guide.title: Which files do I need?
guide.intro: For your taxes you need the complete data of every exchange, broker and wallet you had during the tax year – including accounts that are empty or closed today.

need.transactions: Transaction history or ledger: every booking of the account – buys, sells, swaps, fees, deposits, withdrawals, rewards. This is the most important file; if the platform offers it, it often covers everything else.
need.trades: Trade or order history: the executed trades with price and fee (open or cancelled orders are not needed).
need.transfers: Deposits and withdrawals: crypto (with network and address) and fiat (CHF, EUR, USD) – so transfers between your own accounts are recognised.
need.rewards: Staking, earn, interest, lending, airdrops, cashback: everything you received – this is taxable income.
need.statement: Account or balance statement as of 31.12. (PDF or CSV): the holdings per asset on that day. It is used to check that the history adds up.
need.previousYear: Holdings as of 31.12. of the previous year (or last year's project as a follow-up project): for the opening balance and the earn gap.
need.wallets: Your own wallets (Ledger, Trezor, MetaMask, …): add addresses or xpub in the Wallets tab, or upload the wallet software's export.

tips.period: Period: at least 01.01.–31.12. of the tax year, better from account opening – then holdings and cost bases add up.
tips.everything: If the platform asks: choose all assets, all accounts (spot, earn, futures, sub-accounts) and all columns.
tips.format: Prefer CSV or Excel (XLSX), PDF only for statements. Upload files unchanged – don't open and re-save them in Excel.
tips.closedAccounts: Accounts with a single booking or a small remaining balance count too.

guide.platformsTitle: Examples: where to find the files
guide.platformsNote: Menus change over time – the names are pointers, not a guarantee.

platforms.kraken: Kraken: Documents or History → Export → “Ledgers” (all assets, all fields, CSV); plus the statement as of 31.12.
platforms.binance: Binance: Orders → Transaction History → “Export Transaction Records” (all accounts); plus the account statement as of 31.12.
platforms.bitfinex: Bitfinex: Reports → “Ledgers”, plus “Trades” and “Movements” (deposits and withdrawals).
platforms.coinbase: Coinbase: Profile → Reports or Statements → transaction history (CSV, all assets).
platforms.bitpanda: Bitpanda: History → export transactions (CSV); plus the annual or tax statement.
platforms.revolut: Revolut: Crypto → statement (Excel or CSV) for the whole tax year; plus the crypto tax report if offered.

profile.title: Profile
profile.intro: Your name and canton of residence appear on the statements for the tax authority; the canton determines the form references. Language and number and date format apply to the whole app.

advisor.title: Tax advisor (Treuhänder)
advisor.intro: If someone helps you with your tax return: name and email address. “Send to tax advisor” then sends the statements straight to them.

ai.title: AI plugin
ai.intro: An AI writes mappings for files lazy-koins doesn't know yet and reads PDF statements. It only receives the header row and a few sample rows – before anything is sent, you see exactly what goes out. Without AI, you create mappings by hand.

rates.title: Rates
rates.intro: For valuation, lazy-koins needs rates: exchange rates (ECB), daily closing prices (Binance) and from CoinGecko also coins that Binance doesn't list – without a key through the public API, faster with a free key. You can switch on further providers. The ESTV rate list (Kursliste) with the tax values as of 31.12. is fetched automatically.

wallets.title: Wallets & networks
wallets.intro: With an Etherscan key (one for all EVM chains such as Ethereum, Arbitrum or Polygon) and a Helius key (Solana), lazy-koins fetches holdings and income for your wallet addresses. Bitcoin and Cardano don't need a key.

mail.title: Mail
mail.intro: With a mailer (SMTP), lazy-koins sends the statements straight to your tax advisor. Without a mailer, you copy the text into your own email app.

storage.title: Data folder
storage.intro: Where the database and your original files are stored – in the app's folder or in a folder of your choice, including the sync folder of OneDrive, Google Drive or Proton Drive.

pin.title: PIN
pin.intro: A PIN of 4 to 8 digits locks the app when you open it and after a pause. Only a slow hash is stored, never the PIN itself.

summary.title: Summary
summary.intro: What is set up and what is missing – with what a gap means. Everything can be changed later in Profile and Settings.

profile.languageHint: Applies at once; you can change it any time in your profile.

privacy.title: What leaves this device
privacy.reads: Searching and viewing: only your search text or the entry id – no projects, files or amounts.
privacy.suggestions: Suggestions (when switched on): for each file that still needs a mapping, its header row (the column names) and its file name – never rows, amounts, addresses or folders. Cells that look like data or personal details are left out.
privacy.take: Taking over: only the entry id. The mapping is stored as your own copy; the server does not learn what you use it for.
privacy.never: Never: sign-in data, your e-mail, projects, file contents, ratings or publications.
privacy.offline: Without an address, switched off, or with online lookups switched off, the app never goes online for the library.

bulk.title: Publish {{count}} mappings
bulk.description: Each mapping is reviewed on its own: remove what looks personal, check the JSON – nothing is published before you confirm, and then one after the other.
bulk.quota: Today you can still publish {{remaining}} of {{perDay}} new entries; {{count}} new ones are selected (new versions do not count).
bulk.exceedsToday: That is more new entries than are left today: only {{remaining}} of {{count}} will be accepted, the rest will be refused. Try again tomorrow or select fewer.
bulk.exceedsBudget: At most {{max}} publications per 10 minutes – anything beyond that is refused; try again afterwards.
bulk.alreadyHint: Exactly this mapping is already in the library.

refused.publishLimit: No more new entries today (at most 10 per day) – try again tomorrow.
refused.rateLimited: Too many publications in a short time – wait a few minutes and try again.

block.libraryCopy: This mapping is a copy taken from the library. Someone else's work cannot be published as a new entry – rate the original instead, or publish a mapping of your own.
block.tooLarge: The mapping is too large for the library.
block.reviewFailed: The review of this mapping failed.

bulk.authorHint: Applies to all selected mappings. Empty = "Anonymous"; never your name or e-mail.
bulk.confirm: I have reviewed the {{count}} mappings and want to publish them exactly like this.

settings.title: Coin per ticker
settings.hint: A ticker is not a coin: "OPN" stands for OPEN Ticketing Ecosystem and for Opinion, for example. With a coin set here, its price comes only from the chosen provider – never by ticker from Binance. lazy-koins checks the coin with the provider when saving.
settings.empty: No coin set yet – the ticker applies.

picker.title: Choose the coin for {{asset}}
picker.description: Search the price provider by ticker, name or id and pick the coin you actually hold. Its price history replaces the previous one.
picker.ambiguous: This ticker stands for several coins – check name and rank.

coins.searchFailed: The search at the price provider failed.
coins.saveFailed: The coin could not be saved
coins.removeFailed: The assignment could not be removed
